input.rationale: Small evidence-anchoring supplement: the Behaviour that records NewRaft blocking on the unconsumed FSM queue states its size boundary in terms of the default MaxAppendEntries and the retained log length. Those defaults were re-read from the source (DefaultConfig at config.go:330-340 sets MaxAppendEntries 64, TrailingLogs 10240 and SnapshotThreshold 8192) and are now cited as an anchor on that entry, so the boundary the conditions describe rests on an identified source range rather than on an unsourced assumption. No statement, condition, execution or other record changes.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, NewRaft replays the committed log by pushing one fsmMutateCh message per MaxAppendEntries-sized batch before the FSM goroutine is started; when the committed backlog requires more batches than the queue's 128 slots, the send blocks and NewRaft never returns, so the node never starts.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, no snapshot covering the committed range, and a restored commit index whose replay needs more than 128 batches of MaxAppendEntries entries (DefaultConfig sets MaxAppendEntries 64 and TrailingLogs 10240, so about 8192 retained entries; MaxAppendEntries is validated positive and at most 1024, so the boundary scales with the configured value); observed for 8402 entries (132 batches) with a bounded 15 second wait, against 8002 entries (126 batches) returning in 0-3 ms.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: Receipt f5cb1459db5e418d9a9aa6987ef76dfc (exit 0, fourteen events, no parse loss) settles both comparisons of this question. Comparison 0 is violated by witness event index 11: after restarting the single-voter node with RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, became_leader is false and the final state is Follower across the whole 1500 ms sampling window, with after_latest_index 0 and the matching admission event recording before_latest_index 1 with one server. Comparison 1 holds at evaluated event index 13: the identical restart without the flag reported became_leader true, final state Leader and after_latest_index 1, so the difference tracks the recovery flag rather than restart timing. Source: with an empty latest configuration runFollower takes the 'no known peers, aborting election' branch and never sets Candidate (raft.go:228-232); even on the candidate path quorumSize() would be one while electSelf asks only the servers in that same empty list (raft.go:1087-1094, 1999-2060); and the configuration is empty because restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied past the committed LogConfiguration before the startup scan (api.go:604-620, 724-754). Consequence under the witnessed conditions: a single-voter cluster that restarts with this flag never regains a leader, so duties needing a leader stay pending with no enabled path to completion, since the node's own committed log holds the configuration it would need. The multi-voter variant of the same question was later witnessed under the child question: with a five-voter committed configuration a restarted node kept the stale three-voter configuration and won leadership on two of the committed five votes (receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407, violated at witness event index 22, control holding at 25), so the authority loss is not confined to an empty configuration.
counterevidence: The flag-off control reaches Leader inside the same 1500 ms window, so the non-campaigning is not a general restart delay.

The library deliberately grants votes when the server list is empty (a bootstrap affordance), which explains why such a node still answers vote requests; the witnessed defect is the state it resumes with, not the vote-granting rule.
limitations: This question's own witness is a single-voter configuration with no snapshot; the stale multi-voter election is witnessed under the child question and cited there, not re-observed here.
The window is bounded at 1500 ms against a 50 ms election timeout, so a much later recovery is not excluded.
The snapshot-age configuration variant is witnessed through the configuration observation and the child's election, not through this authority sample.
interpretations.joint_history: Receipt f5cb1459db5e418d9a9aa6987ef76dfc is this question's own execution (single-voter node, no snapshot, wall-clock sampling of the restarted node). Receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 belongs to the child multi-voter question and is cited here only for the follow-on statement that the authority loss also occurs with a stale non-empty configuration. The two are complete executions of different scenarios rather than fragments of one history, and neither is used to establish the other's comparison.

scope.description: Five-voter cluster whose leading node is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs after a snapshot predating the membership change, isolated with one committed voter immediately after the restart; both sides acknowledge a distinct client write, the partition heals, and after eight seconds the event reports whether the two nodes' logs hold different entries at the same index, whether either node applied an entry absent from its own log, and the leadership and acknowledgement outcomes. Run with the flag on and off.
assumptions: A successful Apply is an acknowledgement to the client.
Two nodes holding different entries at the same log index after healing is a violation of log agreement.
Eight seconds is enough for AppendEntries exchange between the two sides.
excluded: Entry contents at the conflict index, which the probe reports as empty strings.
Any claim about durable stores; the in-memory stores are used.

experiment.prefix: The harness reuses the multi-voter scenario construction and the two-sided apply, then scans each side's log store for its own acknowledged entry, compares the two nodes' entries at the isolated side's last index, and emits logs_differ_at_conflict_index with the per-side log and FSM survival flags, the applied-without-log operands, and the leadership and acknowledgement outcomes. No production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns log agreement: after a partition heals, two replicas of the committed configuration must not hold different entries at the same index, especially when both writes were acknowledged to clients.

comparisons.description: After healing, the two nodes must agree at the index where the isolated side wrote; the defect prediction is that they hold different entries there.
Control: with the committed configuration rebuilt the isolated side never writes, so the two logs cannot differ at that index.

experiment.revision_reason: The heal settle is extended from two to eight seconds so a losing suffix has time to be truncated, and the event now carries logs_differ_at_conflict_index, which compares the two nodes' log entries at the index where the isolated side wrote. Scenario, isolation, waits and the two-sided apply are unchanged.

knowledge.statement: At startup the in-memory configuration (r.configurations.latest/committed) is produced only by restoreSnapshot (the latest snapshot's configuration) and by the NewRaft log scan over indexes greater than max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied). With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index before that scan, so a committed LogConfiguration entry at an index <= the restored commit index is never processed and the node keeps the snapshot configuration, or an empty configuration when no snapshot exists.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose latest snapshot predates committed membership changes resumes with the snapshot's configuration: after growing a three-voter cluster to five voters, the restarted leader held configuration index 1 with three servers while its own log's latest configuration was index 14 with five servers, and the same restart without the flag kept index 14 with five servers.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs that keeps a stale, smaller configuration can acknowledge a client write while its support is a minority of the committed configuration: isolated together with one committed voter it became leader and its Apply completed, whereas the same restart without the flag produced no leader on that side and no acknowledgement.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, a restarted node that keeps a stale smaller configuration can both win leadership on a minority of the committed configuration and acknowledge client writes concurrently with the majority side's own leader: in one execution both sides acknowledged a client write while partitioned, and the flag-off control acknowledged only on the majority side.
knowledge.conditions: Committed configuration grown from three to five voters after the restarting node's snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, that partner also cut off from the majority side; a bounded wait for the majority side to hold its own leader before either write; two second apply timeout and two second heal settle.

knowledge.statement: In this scenario and window no acknowledged entry was lost after healing: two seconds after the partition healed, the isolated node and the majority-side leader each still held their own acknowledged entry in their own log store, neither had applied an entry absent from its own log, and the flag-off control's isolated side never acknowledged an entry.

result.summary: Final evidence-anchoring supplement on the startup-blocking behaviour, no new claim. I re-read DefaultConfig to check the premise its conditions assert: config.go:330-340 sets MaxAppendEntries 64, TrailingLogs 10240 and SnapshotThreshold 8192, and the validation at config.go:368-376 bounds MaxAppendEntries to a positive value of at most 1024. The conditions are therefore tightened to name those source ranges and to say the boundary scales with the configured batch size, keeping the measured bracket (8402 entries / 132 batches not returning within 15 s versus 8002 entries / 126 batches returning in 0-3 ms) and the same execution indices. Nothing else in the record changes. Run state at expiry: four questions, each with complete violated comparisons and flag-off controls — restart configuration loss (witness 15, control 18), the stale multi-voter configuration loss with minority leadership, single-side and concurrent two-sided acknowledgements and post-heal log disagreement (22/25, 27/29, 27/29, 27/29), authority loss after restart (11/13), and NewRaft not returning with a large committed backlog against its sub-capacity control (9 vs 7) — plus one resolved gap, one retained durability negative at the two-second window, and knowledge entries for the restart configuration loss, the blocked startup, the authority loss, minority leadership, acknowledged minority writes, the post-heal disagreement and the durability negative.
